title: Lambda Red-mediated Recombineering in the Attaching and Effacing Pathogen Escherichia albertii
author: Egan, Ramirez, et al.
materials: Our initial attempts at recombineering in E. albertii using pKD46 were largely unsuccessful or non-reproducible (data not shown). Previous research has shown that recombineering efficiency is significantly enhanced in the related bacterium E. coli when the lambda red genes are expressed from the pSIM rather than the pKD family of plasmids [28]. The pSIM family of plasmids is derived from the defective lambda prophage in which the minimal lambda red recombinase operon, consisting of the genes gam, bet, and exo, is expressed from the pL promoter under the transcriptional control of the thermolabile CI857 lambda repressor [28]. At low temperatures ranging from 30–34 °C CI857 is active and binds to the operator site thereby sterically hindering the promoter and preventing transcription. A thermal upshift to 42 °C reversibly denatures the CI857 repressor thereby inactivating it and leading to the derepression of the gam, bet, and exo genes thereby inducing a temporary hyperrecombinogenic state in the bacterium [28]. When such a bacterium is transformed with dsDNA or oligonucleotides that possess two terminal arms of ~40–50 nucleotides of homology to a target gene the lambda red recombinase promotes the replacement of the endogenous allele with the exogenous allele. Transcription from pL promoter can be shut off by transferring the cultures back to 30 °C at which the CI857 repressor renatures and binds to the operator to prevent further transcription. Reversible repression by CI857 prevents the unregulated expression of the lambda red genes, which has previously been shown to be mutagenic [25].

To evict the cat cassette, the recombinants were transformed with the plasmid pFT-K [104]. Transformation was done essentially as described above. pFT-K is a thermolabile replicon that confers temperature-sensitive resistance to kanamycin (25 μg/ml) and expresses the flp recombinase under the control of the tetracycline repressor (TetR) of the transposon Tn10. All the KanR transformants that were observed were pooled together into 20 ml of LB supplemented with kanamycin and grown overnight at 30 °C/250 rpm. The overnight grown culture was diluted 100 fold into fresh identical media and incubated at 30 °C under static conditions for 24 h. The following day the FLP recombinase was induced by diluting the overnight culture 4 fold in 20 ml of LB supplemented with unautoclaved chlorotetracycline, at a range of concentrations (20–200 μg/ml), and growing overnight at 30 °C under static conditions. Chlorotetracycline binds to and inactivates the TetR repressor thereby derepressing the flp gene. FLP recombinase, in turn, recognizes and catalyzes the site-specific recombination between the two direct repetitive FRT sites to evict the bracketed cat resistance cassette, leaving behind a solitary residual FRT site. As a consequence, the engineered bacterial excisant becomes resensitized to chloramphenicol. After overnight induction of the cultures, a loopful of bacteria was streaked onto nonselective LB plates and incubated overnight at 42 °C to cure the thermolabile plasmid. The next day ~36 independently isolated colonies were spot-streaked onto LB, LB + Cm, and LB + Kan and incubated overnight at 30 °C to screen for the CmS excisants that had also been cured of the plasmid (KanS). If the excisant had not been cured of the plasmid then the CmS isolate was re-streaked onto fresh LB plates and incubated for another night at 42 °C to cure the plasmid. The genotype of the excisants was further verified by PCR as described above.

steps.title: Introduce pSIM6 plasmid into E. albertii
steps.instruction: Streak E. albertii strain Albert 19982T onto LB plates and incubate overnight at 37 °C. Pick a single colony into 5 ml LB with ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and grow overnight at 37 °C, 250 rpm. Sub‑culture 100‑fold into 30 ml LB with ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and grow to OD₆₀₀ ≈0.6–0.8. Make cells electrocompetent (see step 3) and electroporate 90 µl of cells with 100 ng pSIM6 plasmid (or pKD46 as control) using ~1.8–2.5 kV. Recover in 1 ml LB for 3 h at 30 °C, then plate 200 µl on LB + ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and incubate overnight at 30 °C. Pick two independent colonies, grow each in 5 ml LB + ampicillin (100 µg/ml) overnight at 30 °C, 250 rpm and store at –80 °C or use directly for recombineering.

steps.title: Induce lambda red recombinase expression
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single pSIM6‑carrying colony into 5 ml LB + ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and grow overnight at 30 °C, 250 rpm. Dilute 100‑fold into 30 ml fresh LB + ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and grow at 30 °C, 250 rpm to OD₆₀₀ 0.6–1.0. Heat‑shock the culture in a 42 °C water bath with shaking (250 rpm) for 1 h to induce the gam‑bet‑exo operon. (Earlier experiments used 7.5, 15, or 30 min inductions; the optimized protocol uses 1 h.) Immediately chill the culture by swirling in an ice‑water bath for ~2 min before proceeding to electrocompetent‑cell preparation.

steps.title: Prepare electrocompetent cells
steps.instruction: Harvest the induced culture by centrifugation at 4 °C, 4100 rpm for 10 min. Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1 ml ice‑cold 10 % glycerol. Add 29 ml ice‑cold 10 % glycerol (final volume 30 ml) and centrifuge again at 4 °C, 4100 rpm for 10 min. Repeat glycerol wash a minimum of three times, each time resuspending in 1 ml ice‑cold 10 % glycerol, centrifuging, and discarding supernatant. After the final wash, resuspend the pellet in 400 µl ice‑cold 10 % glycerol. Aliquot 90 µl of this electrocompetent suspension into pre‑chilled microcentrifuge tubes; keep on ice until electroporation.

steps.title: Amplify and purify resistance cassette
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µl HiFi Taq PCR using chimeric primers that contain ~50‑nt homology arms (up‑ and downstream of the target locus) fused to ~19‑20 nt sequences annealing to pKD3 (cat) or pKD13 (kan). PCR cycling: 94 °C 5 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C 0.5 min, 43 °C 0.5 min, 68 °C 2 min; final extension 72 °C 7 min; hold at 15 °C. Verify product size by 1 % agarose gel electrophoresis. Concentrate the amplicon with Zymo DNA Clean & Concentrator‑25 into 25 µl elution buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5, 0.1 mM EDTA). Precipitate by adding 2 µl glycogen (20 mg/ml), 20 µl sodium acetate (pH 5.2), and 900 µl cold 100 % ethanol (‑20 °C); mix and incubate at ‑20 °C for ≥30 min. Centrifuge 4 °C, 16 000 rpm, 15 min; discard supernatant; wash pellet 3× with 500 µl 70 % ethanol, centrifuging 4 °C, 16 000 rpm, 5 min each wash. Air‑dry pellet and resuspend in 10 µl molecular‑grade water. Store at ‑20 °C until use.

steps.title: Electroporate linear DNA into cells
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 µg of the ethanol‑precipitated PCR product to 90 µl of the chilled electrocompetent cells (negative control receives no DNA). Incubate on ice for ~1 min. Transfer mixture to a pre‑chilled electroporation cuvette and electroporate at 1.8–2.5 kV (≈2.5 kV gave higher recombination rates). Immediately add 1 ml LB to the cuvette, transfer to a tube containing an additional 9 ml LB, and incubate at 37 °C, 250 rpm for at least 16 h (overnight).

steps.title: Recover and select recombinants
steps.instruction: After overnight outgrowth, transfer 1.5 ml of culture to a microcentrifuge tube, centrifuge 16 000 rpm, 2 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 150–200 µl LB. Plate the suspension on LB agar containing the appropriate antibiotic: chloramphenicol 3.125–25 µg/ml (for cat cassettes) or kanamycin 15–22.5 µg/ml (for kan cassettes). Incubate plates at 37 °C for 1–2 days until colonies appear.

steps.title: Verify allelic replacement by PCR
steps.instruction: Pick individual colonies into 50 µl LB and grow 3 h at 37 °C. Use 2 µl of the culture as template in a locus‑specific PCR (primer pairs listed in Table 2). Run 4 µl of each PCR product on a 1 % agarose gel stained with ethidium bromide and visualise under a transilluminator. Confirm the expected size shift (e.g., wild‑type ler ~1.8 kb → Δler::cat ~2.5 kb; grlRA ~1.8 kb → ΔgrlRA::kan ~2.3 kb; hfq ~527 bp → Δhfq::cat ~1.27 kb).

steps.title: Cure pSIM6 plasmid from recombinants
steps.instruction: Streak verified recombinants onto LB agar containing chloramphenicol 6.25 µg/ml and/or kanamycin 22.5 µg/ml and incubate overnight at 42 °C. The next day, pick several colonies from each sector and patch onto LB + Cm/Kan plates and LB + Amp plates; incubate at 30 °C overnight. Colonies that are Ampicillin‑sensitive (AmpS) have lost pSIM6.

steps.title: Introduce pFT‑K plasmid for cassette eviction
steps.instruction: Transform the pSIM6‑cured Δler::cat (or other) recombinants with plasmid pFT‑K using the same electroporation conditions as in step 5 (90 µl cells, 1.5 µg pFT‑K, 1.8–2.5 kV). Recover in 1 ml LB for 1 h at 30 °C, then plate on LB + kanamycin (25 µg/ml) and incubate at 30 °C overnight to select pFT‑K transformants.

steps.title: Induce FLP recombinase with chlorotetracycline
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single pFT‑K transformant into 20 ml LB + kanamycin (25 µg/ml) and grow overnight at 30 °C, 250 rpm. Dilute the overnight culture 100‑fold into fresh LB + kanamycin (25 µg/ml) and incubate statically at 30 °C for 24 h. Then dilute the culture 4‑fold into 20 ml LB containing unautoclaved chlorotetracycline at the desired concentration (20, 50, 100, or 200 µg/ml) and incubate overnight (≈16 h) at 30 °C, static. Chlorotetracycline inactivates TetR, derepressing flp expression; FLP mediates recombination between the two FRT sites, excising the cat cassette and leaving a single FRT scar.

steps.title: Cure pFT‑K plasmid
steps.instruction: After FLP induction, streak a loopful of culture onto non‑selective LB agar and incubate overnight at 42 °C to eliminate the temperature‑sensitive pFT‑K plasmid. Repeat streaking onto fresh LB at 42 °C if colonies remain kanamycin‑resistant.

steps.title: Screen and confirm excisants
steps.instruction: Pick ~36 individual colonies from the cured plates and spot‑streak each onto three plates: LB alone, LB + chloramphenicol (3.125 µg/ml), and LB + kanamycin (25 µg/ml). Incubate at 30 °C overnight. Colonies that are chloramphenicol‑sensitive (CmS) and kanamycin‑sensitive (KanS) are successful excisants. Verify loss of the cat cassette and presence of the residual FRT site by locus‑specific PCR using the same primer pairs as in step 7 (expected product ~1.55 kb for Δler::FRT versus ~1.8 kb wild‑type).
